title: Returned Income Annuities Payments: Recording Rule
content:
**Rule.** A payment on an Ashgrove Income Annuities contract that is returned by the bank or the postal service reverses only the payment it names. Each returned payment is recorded once against the payment it reverses. The returned installment is held under the rules on proof of life and suspension of payments. A deposit rejected because the account holder is deceased is treated as a report of death.

**What the records show.** The return is matched to one issued payment on the contract's activity history. Whether that payment already has a return recorded against it is read from the activity history, not from a caller's account.

| Situation on the activity history | Effect |
|---|---|
| Issued payment with no return recorded against it, now returned | One return is recorded against that payment and the installment is held |
| Issued payment already carrying a recorded return | No second return is recorded for it |
| Deposit rejected because the account holder is deceased | Treated as a report of death |

*Hypothetical illustration.* Two monthly payments, for 1 April and 1 May, were deposited; the bank returns the 1 May deposit. Only the 1 May payment is reversed and held; the 1 April payment stands. If the same 1 May return is reported again, it is not recorded a second time.
